finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::"read-only" guarantee advertised by the new docs page rests on a bypassable sql keyword denylist
evidence: Verified against the supplied sources: sql-validator.ts:1-13 and 38-58 implement only a first-token SELECT/WITH check plus a fixed keyword denylist, and datasource.service.ts `executeQuery` wraps the raw `dto.query` in `SELECT * FROM (...) AS _q LIMIT`. Nothing blocks side-effecting or SSRF-capable function calls reachable from a SELECT (`pg_read_file`, `lo_import`, `dblink`, `pg_terminate_backend`, `setval`, `pg_sleep`), and COPY/DO/CALL/MERGE are indeed absent from the denylist — so the core technical claim is correct about the code as written. The claim's secondary "validator/executor text divergence" argument is overstated: the comment/string stripping makes the validator see *more* text (false positives), and I could not derive a bypass from it. Impact is bounded — every path goes through `assertMember`, and the credentials are ones a workspace member entered for their own DB, so this is member-vs-member privilege reach rather than an open hole, and the docs line at datasources.md:37 reads more like a UI statement ("can't edit, sort, or filter the cells in place") than a security guarantee; sql-validator.ts is also untouched by this PR.
